sentences.text: But ordinary derivors are not enough, for two reasons.
First, some functors keep only part of the elements, whereas a derivor keeps the whole carrier:
graduation keeps, as cells of dimension K and sort s, only the cells that are their own K source.
Second, some domains cannot be expressed by any term.
Discretization interprets a higher composition by its first argument, which is always defined.
And yet, in the discretized algebra, two cells must be composable only when they are equal:
a set becomes a discrete category, in which a cell can only be composed with itself.
